input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG EMPL - EMPLOYMENT, SOCIAL AFFAIRS AND INCLUSION. Summary: Business Support for Europass and Esco. Description: The purpose of this Service Contract is to provide technical support to the European Commission in two activities in the field of labour mobility. Firstly, it covers the continuous improvement of Europass, the European framework of online tools and information, which seek to support better understanding and communication of skills and qualifications. Tasks include the identification of business needs and solutions, the creation and clarification of requirements for new features and releases (the subsequent steps of technical analysis and IT development are not part of this contract), the interactions and discussions with the Europass Advisory Group (Europass AG) and the National Europass Centres (NEC), the monitoring and evaluation of the latter-s performance and the continuous update and completion of content on the Europass platform. Secondly, it covers the development and implementation of datasets for interoperability in the labour market and the area of education and training, the mapping of semantic assets in order to increase interoperability between systems and the strategic design and continuous improvement of ESCO (European classification of Skills, Competences and Occupations). <br> Doc Title: Business support for Europass and ESCO <br> Contract Type: services. The local police fulfills seven basic functionalities: community work, reception, intervention, victim treatment, local investigation, public order and traffic. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN FREE TRADE ORGANISATION, FINANCIAL MECHANISM OFFICE. Summary: Fund Operator for the Social Dialogue and Decent Work Programme under the Norwegian Financial Mechanism 2021-2028. Description: Through the Norway Grants, Norway works closely with partners in 13 EU Member States in Central and Southern Europe and the Baltic States, to contribute to the reduction of social and economic disparities in the European Economic Area (EEA) and the strengthening of bilateral cooperation. Support to social dialogue and decent work has been a key priority for the Norway Grants since 2004. The Agreement between Norway and the European Union on the Norwegian Financial Mechanism (2021-2028) sets aside €14,640,000 for a fund for social dialogue and decent work. The Social Dialogue and Decent Work Fund (SDDW Fund) is made available to actors in all the Norway Grants Beneficiary States, to strengthen social dialogue between workers- organisations, employers- organisations and public authorities and promote decent work. The Financial Mechanism Office (FMO) is the Brussels-based secretariat for the Norway Grants. The FMO is affiliated to the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and reports to the Foreign Ministry of Norway. The decision-making body of the Norway Grants is the Foreign Ministry of Norway. The FMO has been entrusted with the role of Programme Operator (PO) of the SDDW Fund. The role of the PO is to select and contract the Fund Operator, monitor compliance with the legal framework of the SDDW Fund and follow up on the progress and quality of fund implementation. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DGEM. Summary: Survey of the General Belgian Public Concerning the Use of Insecticides (Tp18) and Repellents (Tp19). Description: This market concerns the use made by the general public of insecticide and repellent biocidal products (TP18 and 19) via an online survey carried out throughout Belgium. This survey will be supported by qualitative information coming from focus groups to which more specific questions will be submitted (see technical requirements). The goal is to determine the motivations pushing users to use these types of products, to identify which types of products are used and how. An important part of the investigation also aims to determine whether the instructions and risk reduction measures detailed on the label or instructions for use are read, understood and followed. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DEPARTMENT OF CULTURE, YOUTH AND MEDIA. Summary: Research Integrity in Youth Work. Description: The Department of Culture, Youth and Media wants to conduct research into the theme of integrity in youth work. Integrity is a social theme that is receiving a lot of attention. There is already a strong focus on subsidized youth work creating a safe environment for children and young people, but also focusing on learning about issues and reconnecting through a recovery-oriented approach. Furthermore, further expectations regarding integrity have been formulated in recent years Flemish Government. The Youth Decree of 23 November 2023 defines an integrity policy as a set of policy instruments at organizational level with the objectives: • the preservation and promotion of the individual physical, psychological and sexual integrity of persons; • promoting the integrity of the organization as a whole and the integrity of its youth workers. Summary: The Organization of a Targeted Survey on the Daily Travel of Belgians Using a Dynamic Questionnaire. Description: This contract concerns the organization of a targeted survey on the daily travel of Belgians using a dynamic questionnaire. It aims more specifically to obtain data on the movements of Belgians, adults (18 years and over) and children (6 years-17 years) and who are not or no longer available from other sources, collected in the past via large-scale surveys carried out by or in collaboration with the FPS Mobility and Transport (MOBEL, BELDAM surveys and more recently MONITOR). This survey will be carried out online by a survey office with a sufficiently large panel of respondents. The FPS Mobility and Transport will analyze the data with the aim of describing mobility habits at the level of the Belgian population and also according to different general characteristics (gender, age group, region of residence, etc.). The aggregated results of the analyzes will be the subject of oral or written publications by the FPS Mobility and Transport. Category (CPV code): Survey conduction services (79311200). Two pillars are central: on the one hand an international benchmark and on the other hand a case study. The purpose of the benchmark is to gain insight into the instruments (may be broader than permits) or techniques (regulatory or not) that other representative Member States or regions use to achieve the same objectives as those of Title II of the VLAREM, namely the prevention or limitation of unacceptable nuisance and risks arising from operations, and the positive and negative elements that are experienced, such as complexity. The purpose of the case study is to investigate how unacceptable nuisance and risks for ZS can be limited by legally anchoring a Flemish ZS policy. The research should provide insights, including on the basis of a comparative legal study, into how flexible and legally certain environmental standards or conditions can be anchored, taking into account, among other things, the standstill principle. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG COMP - COMPETITION. Summary: Study on Modern Pricing and Risks of Collusion. Description: DG COMP is working on a follow-up to the comprehensive 2024 report: “Protecting competition in a changing world: Evidence on the evolution of competition in the EU during the past 25 years”. This report identified important changes over the past 25 years in the competitive environment (rising concentration, markups and profits, declining business dynamism). It also identified a number of likely structural and institutional drivers of those changes (rise of intangible investments, globalisation, regulation and M&A). The 2024 report did however not explore whether changes in management practices (strategies and tactics) may also have contributed to some of the detected trends. The present study seeks to address this gap by exploring whether the rise of modern pricing and revenue management strategies and tactics may have partly contributed to some of the observed changes in the competitive environment, inter alia by increasing the risk of collusion. <br> Doc Title: Study on modern pricing and risks of collusion <br> Contract Type: services. Published Date: 2025-10-20. Closing Date: 2025-11-17. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: European Commission

input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DEPARTMENT OF WELFARE, PUBLIC HEALTH AND FAMILY. Summary: Development of Support Resources and Scripts for the Efficient Use of Resources to Prevent Tiger Mosquito-Transmitted Infectious Diseases in Flanders. Description: Since the start of national mosquito surveillance and monitoring in 2022, an increasing spread of tiger mosquitoes (Aedes albopictus) in Flanders has been reported annually. Local control keeps populations under control, but is not successful in order to completely eradicate those tiger mosquito populations, the dense buildings in Flanders make us extra vulnerable to invasion by the tiger mosquito. At the same time, we have seen an increase in outbreaks of mosquito-borne diseases worldwide in recent years. Travel to endemic areas causes an increase in the number of imported disease cases in Belgium and Flanders. Because the tiger mosquito established itself locally in Flanders, this can lead to autochthonous transmission of previously tropical diseases. This is a worrying development for which we in Flanders can better prepare. After all, the risk of local transmission of these mosquito diseases depends on future heat periods, the investment in, and efficiency of, surveillance, monitoring and control. This government contract specifically focuses on: • Developing scenarios, clear procedures and practical tools for local interventions with regard to the prevention of disease transmission by the tiger mosquito in imported cases and native cases. • Drawing up a risk mapping (both in time and space) based on scientifically supported risk factors, which reduce the risk of local dense tiger mosquitoes.... input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG COMP - COMPETITION. Summary: Study on Modern Pricing and Risks of Collusion. Description: DG COMP is working on a follow-up to the comprehensive 2024 report: “Protecting competition in a changing world: Evidence on the evolution of competition in the EU during the past 25 years”. This report identified important changes over the past 25 years in the competitive environment (rising concentration, markups and profits, declining business dynamism). It also identified a number of likely structural and institutional drivers of those changes (rise of intangible investments, globalisation, regulation and M&A). The 2024 report did however not explore whether changes in management practices (strategies and tactics) may also have contributed to some of the detected trends.
